faq.whiteScreenQuestion: I have a white screen when I want to read the Bible
faq.whiteScreenAnswer: This bug seems to appear on certain phone models (Tecno, Infinix ...).If you have an Android 6 or lower version, you can update Android System WebView in the Play Store.
Si l'application est lente sur votre tél:
If the application is slow on your phone, I'm sorry. Bible Strong uses lexicon and dictionary databases that contain thousands of entries. Generally recent phones have good performance on the application. 

I will optimize some parts of the app like the lexicon and the dictionary in the future.
L'application prend beaucoup de place: The application takes up a lot of space
J'ai fait le choix de vous fournir le le:
I have chosen to provide you with the lexicon, the Bibles and the offline dictionary to facilitate quick access. 

The advantage is of course the fast and offline access of all your information, the drawback is the size of the application. 

 ~ 25Mo for the dictionary, ~ 30Mo for the Hebrew lexicon. Each bible weighs around ~ 5MB.

 In the whole application can reach up to 200MB, so make sure you have room.
faq.bugNoticedAnswer: To avoid overloading the team's solo developer, only sponsors can submit bugs using the link "Submit a bug " in the "Plus " section.
faq.ideaAnswer: To avoid overloading the team's solo developer, only sponsors can submit ideas using the link "Submit an idea " in the "Plus " section.
who-are-you:
Very good question ! My name is Stéphane, I am 30 years old, I have been designing and developing web and mobile for 10 years. 

I come from Martinique, I am a Seventh-day Adventist and I am currently living in New Zealand with my wife. 

I decided to create this application because I couldn't find one that met my needs in terms of ease of use and ergonomics for studying the Bible. I wanted to organize my verses, write my studies, take my notes, see them directly integrated into my bible, create my tags, etc. 

I therefore wish to contribute to the building by offering a free application, funded by donations and sponsors. :).

Prévoyez-vous la date du retour du Chris: Do you foresee the date of Christ's return?
Non. La Bible dit que quant au jour et à: No. The Bible says that as to the day and time of Christ's return, no one knows. See Matthew 24; 50. Furthermore, Christ's return will only come after other prophetic achievements have occurred - and we also don't know when they will happen. The purpose of the timeline is not to predict when exactly future events will occur, but rather to show the reliability of the Bible as a historical document, its reliability in prophecy and as a tool for in-depth study of the Bible.

versionCatalog.style.wordForWord.descrip: This approach stays as close as practical to the wording and structure of the source text. It is useful for precise study, but can sometimes feel less natural to read.
versionCatalog.style.balanced.descriptio: This approach balances fidelity to the original wording with fluent reading in contemporary language.
versionCatalog.style.thoughtForThought.d: This approach prioritizes communicating the meaning of a sentence clearly, even when its wording differs from the form of the source text.
versionCatalog.style.paraphrase.descript: This approach reformulates the message more freely to make it easier to understand. It suits accessible reading better than detailed word study.

offlineSetup.bibleFacts.jehovah: “Jehovah” combines the consonants YHWH with vowels indicating that Adonai should be read instead: it is probably not the ancient pronunciation.
offlineSetup.bibleFacts.johnLove: In John 21, while Peter is speaking with Jesus, Jesus changes from agapaō to phileō in his third question.
offlineSetup.bibleFacts.lucifer: In Isaiah 14, “Lucifer” is Latin for “morning star,” in a satire about the king of Babylon.
offlineSetup.bibleFacts.christTitle: “Christ” is not Jesus’ family name: christos is a Greek title meaning “anointed,” equivalent to “Messiah.”
offlineSetup.bibleFacts.jesusJoshua: Jesus and Joshua share the same Greek name, Iēsous. In Hebrews 4:8, only the context tells us that Joshua is meant.
offlineSetup.bibleFacts.hosanna: “Hosanna” originally meant “save, please,” before also becoming an acclamation of praise.
offlineSetup.bibleFacts.sheol: Sheol is the realm of the dead in the Hebrew Bible. Consistently translating it as “hell” adds ideas that developed much later.
offlineSetup.bibleFacts.gehenna: “Gehenna” comes from the name of a valley near Jerusalem, which later became an image of judgment.
offlineSetup.bibleFacts.adamAdamah: In Genesis 2, adam and adamah form a wordplay: the human is taken from the humus, or ground.
offlineSetup.bibleFacts.adamSide: Adam’s “rib” translates tsela, a word that usually means “side.” “Rib” remains possible, but it is not the word’s only meaning.
offlineSetup.bibleFacts.shalom: Shalom means more than “peace”: its word family evokes what is whole, complete, or restored. In Nehemiah 6:15, a verb from the same root describes the wall as “finished.”
offlineSetup.bibleFacts.strongNumbers: Strong’s numbers are named after James Strong, who published his concordance in 1890. Jack Cochrane and Germain Chouinard created a French-language adaptation for the Segond Bible.
offlineSetup.bibleFacts.psalm119: Psalm 119’s 176 verses form 22 stanzas: eight verses for each letter of the Hebrew alphabet.
